batches.duplicateHandling: Four source note IDs were exact replays from the earlier batch. They were linked to existing items and did not increase occurrence counts.

items.title: Lead Quiet Games with familiar named games
items.normalizedFinding: Begin Quiet Games with familiar formats: I Spy, Charades, Would You Rather, Animal Guessing with yes/no questions, and Alphabet Story. Place optional categories and variations inside each familiar game.
items.expectedBehavior: A tester can choose a familiar game immediately and then use optional suggestions or variations.
items.duplicateMergeRationale: Both notes request I Spy; the second expands the same discoverability and list-organization need.

items.title: Group Mad Libs stories under a Mad Libs submenu
items.normalizedFinding: Collect individual Mad Libs stories beneath one Mad Libs entry and submenu.
items.expectedBehavior: Quiet Games shows one Mad Libs entry that opens the available stories.

items.title: Add a child-appropriate Gross Would You Rather set
items.normalizedFinding: Add a gross-humor Would You Rather variation using absurd bodily or food concepts while excluding crass or inappropriate material.
items.expectedBehavior: Would You Rather offers a clearly labeled, reviewed, child-appropriate gross-humor prompt set.

items.title: Add Race Like an Animal as an active game
items.normalizedFinding: Add a race in which participants choose an animal and imitate its movement. Suggested animals include kangaroo, cheetah, rabbit, and frog.
items.expectedBehavior: The activity explains animal selection, a safe race area, and animal-style movement.

items.title: Add Indoor Marco Polo with pillows
items.normalizedFinding: Add an indoor Marco Polo activity that incorporates pillows.
items.expectedBehavior: The activity supplies ready-to-use setup and play instructions and is safety-reviewed before activation.
items.safetyRedesign: Eyes remain open; players walk only; the adult supervises as a stationary caller. Pillows are flat boundary/island markers only, never thrown, used for face covering, piled, or jumped on. Setup clears stairs, furniture edges, cords, pets, and fragile objects, and play stops if it becomes chaotic.

items.title: Minimize and compact the home screen
items.normalizedFinding: Keep KinPlay at the upper-left, place a concise one-line descriptor beside it, remove the What fits now instructional section, and move the six-category grid upward. Defer richer graphics and animated characters to later development.
items.expectedBehavior: The first screen presents identity, purpose, and category choices with minimal copy and no unnecessary vertical gap.

items.title: Show suitable-place cues on category cards
items.normalizedFinding: Replace each category card’s game count with a concise list of suitable play locations, including waiting-room cues for quiet activities and backyard or living-room cues for high-energy activities.
items.expectedBehavior: A parent can choose a category from the current setting without interpreting an inventory count.

items.title: Label Quality Time activities by group suitability
items.normalizedFinding: Mark the Quality Time category and each activity as intended for one-on-one play, group play, or both.
items.expectedBehavior: A parent can identify participant fit before opening or starting an activity.

items.title: Include activities as well as games
items.normalizedFinding: Treat suitable activities as first-class content alongside games, including drawing, coloring, and painting.
items.expectedBehavior: Discovery and category language accommodate both games and activities that support family engagement and children’s creativity.

items.title: Make low-cognitive-load parent support a product requirement
items.normalizedFinding: KinPlay should supply ready-to-use inspiration, choices, and facilitation so an exhausted or overwhelmed parent does not have to invent the activity. The intended outcome is family interaction, closeness, and children’s creativity and imagination.
items.expectedBehavior: Core flows provide immediately usable choices and guidance while minimizing decisions, setup work, and creative effort required from the parent.
